label: K-12 school district
description: A public school district, charter network or private school system: elementary, middle and high schools, district transportation (school buses), nutrition services and athletics; student information, learning and parent-notification systems, 1:1 devices, panic-alarm and visitor-management apps, building automation and door access; and the state education agency, police and parents it answers to.

vocabulary.facility: the district (its schools, bus routes, central office and stadium)
vocabulary.public: students, parents and families, staff and visitors
vocabulary.frontline: building principals, teachers, school resource officers, bus drivers, front-office staff, school nurses, custodians
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the district emergency operations center (EOC) at the central office

it: student information system (SIS): PowerSchool, Infinite Campus, Skyward, Aeries or Synergy
learning management: Google Classroom / Workspace for Education, Canvas, Schoology or Seesaw
identity and SSO rostering (Google Workspace or Entra ID, Clever or ClassLink)
1:1 Chromebooks and iPads with MDM (Google Admin, Jamf) and a content filter
district website / CMS and the VoIP phone system
ERP / finance / HR / payroll and the nutrition point-of-sale
visitor management, anonymous tip line and threat-assessment case management
transportation routing (Transfinder, Edulog) and student ridership card scans
ot: PACS card access and door-lock status
silent panic-alarm app linked to 911 (Alyssa's Law type)

roles.name: Director of School Safety / District Emergency Manager (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Activates the district EOC, sets incident objectives, calls lockdown, secure, hold, evacuate or shelter, and liaises with police and fire.

roles.name: Superintendent (Policy Group chair)
roles.description: Decides closures and early release, district-wide statements, the board briefing and, with counsel and the insurer, any ransom question.

roles.name: Building Principal (site incident commander)
roles.description: Owns the first actions at the school: lockdown, evacuation, student accountability and staff assignments until responders take over.

roles.name: School Resource Officer / School Police Chief
roles.description: Owns the initial law-enforcement response, threat investigation and the liaison to city police or the sheriff.

roles.name: Chief Technology Officer (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the SIS, LMS, phones, Wi-Fi and 1:1 devices, containment, vendor coordination and the MS-ISAC / K12 SIX / CISA liaison.

roles.name: Chief Communications Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Owns parent notification through the mass-notification system, social media, media staging and rumor control.

roles.name: Assistant Superintendent for Student Services
roles.description: Owns student accountability and reunification, IEP and 504 accommodations, health services, counseling and the crisis team.

roles.name: Director of Transportation
roles.description: Owns buses, routes, driver accountability, AVL and the buses for relocation and reunification.

outsideParties: city police, the county sheriff, fire and EMS
county emergency management and the public-health department
the state education agency and its school-safety center
the state fusion center and the state tip line
the FBI field office and CISA (K-12 cybersecurity and protective security advisors)
the U.S. Secret Service National Threat Assessment Center
the Department of Education (REMS TA Center, Student Privacy Policy Office)
the SIS vendor, the mass-notification vendor and the managed IT provider
the cyber insurer (often a state school-insurance pool) and the DFIR firm
the bus contractor and neighboring districts (buses and sites under mutual aid)
the school board and the teachers' union
mediaChannels: a parents' Facebook group and Nextdoor
student TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram posts (threat screenshots, rumors)
the local TV assignment desk and the local newspaper
the district's own mass-notification messages and website banner

sceneAnchors.control: inside a school district emergency operations center: staff at folding tables with laptops and radios, a wall map of school locations and bus routes, binders of emergency plans, fluorescent light
sceneAnchors.exterior: a high school campus from the parking lot: a brick two-story building with a covered main entrance and visitor vestibule, a football stadium with light towers behind it, a police SUV at the curb, overcast daylight

noiseExamples: a bus running twenty minutes late on a morning route
a teacher locked out of Google Classroom
a fire alarm from a science-lab experiment
a parent disputing an absence in the parent portal
a Chromebook cart that will not charge
a lunch-line POS that will not read student IDs
pressureExamples: a Snapchat screenshot of a threat that names 'tomorrow' and a high school
a parents' Facebook group saying the district is hiding something
a reporter asking whether student IEP and health records were stolen
a board member demanding to know why schools are open
parents arriving at a locked school to take their children home
the state education agency asking for an incident report
